answer: A river timber yard stopped cloned booking bots by opening one weighbridge only at dawn. Each haulier must drive a real load onto the plate and take a single-use comet token bound to that mass, an axle photo, and the stencilled bay number. A fake fleet cannot mint tokens without renting trucks, burning diesel, and queuing in the cold, so identity has a cash cost. Clerks match delivered mass within two percent and reject any token stamped after sunrise or reused at a second gate. When masses diverge, the yard voids the token and slashes the haulier bond, clearing empty accounts in six nights.
